pages.title: autoGT ground truth: quality overview
lines: Question: how good is the ground truth autoGT generates from nuScenes, and where does it fail?
What 'good' can mean here. autoGT labels nothing itself: it rasterises the HD map, the human 3D box annotations, the ego poses and the radar returns
into BEV layers. So four things can be checked: (1) faithfulness to those sources, (2) physical and bookkeeping consistency, (3) plausibility against the
camera image, (4) where it breaks. What cannot be checked is accuracy against an independent truth: no lidar is on disk, and the annotations ARE the truth
that is inherited (their own error is not estimated here).
Versions and data behind the numbers
generator signature 15efbde2d1: moving boxes at the CAMERA time (decision 2026-10-31). The rebuild of nuScenes trainval with it is running: 480 of 850
sequences were stored when this was written.
[T] complete trainval run, 850 sequences / 34,149 keyframes, 0 failed, with the earlier signature 7fe1149566 (boxes at the annotation time; everything
except the positions of moving boxes is identical). Report PDF autogt/reports/autogt_report_v1.0-trainval_2026-10-30.pdf.
[M] nuScenes mini at the final signature: 10 sequences, 404 keyframes, all checks + the leave-one-radar-out radar test (autogt_report_v1.0-mini_2026-10-31.pdf).
[S] a scan of the stored GT of the final signature: 458 sequences, 9246 keyframes (every 2nd keyframe), split by map and weather. These are the
sequences with the lowest numbers: Boston-heavy and daytime; night sequences are shown from mini (scene-1077 / 1094 / 1100) until the rebuild reaches them.
Pictures: 96 random keyframes (thumbnails), 38 examples with 4 panels each, 7 full-resolution camera close-ups. Captions say 'Observed' where I looked at
the picture and described what I saw, and 'Selected by' where the picture was chosen by a rule and not inspected individually.
Verdict in one paragraph
Where the map exists, the GT is consistent and plausible: boxes enclose the cars and pedestrians in the camera image (day, rain, night), map lines lie on
the paint within a few decimetres (Boston close-ups), moving vehicles stand on the drivable area (97.6 %), the velocity field is consistent with the radar (radial error median
0.2 m/s) and nothing that is stationary drifts (0.00 cm). The weak spots are all INHERITED or modelling limits, not generator bugs: map holes (no road under
the ego car in 0.5 % of the keyframes, Boston construction sequences), roads outside the 2D map (2.4 % of the moving vehicles drive outside the drivable
area, 6-9 % in two Singapore maps; the two cases inspected are elevated roads), the 2D occlusion mask (hides 11 % of boxes the annotators rate as clearly
visible), 22 % of the boxes off the ego ground plane (hills, overpasses), and the radial-only radar check of velocity. The consequence for training is in
section 4 of autogt/AGENTS.md.

pages.title: Quality by condition
lines: Quality by condition [S] (every 2nd keyframe of the sequences stored at the final signature; ratios of sums over the keyframes)
group                      sequences keyframes boxes/kf  ignored  moving vehicles   pedestrians on    boxes >0.5 m off   visible boxes     ego off
share    on drivable area  a map surface     the ground plane   marked occluded   the map
How to read it
ignored share = boxes without any lidar / radar point / all boxes in range; moving vehicles = known velocity > 1 m/s; pedestrians on a map surface = centre cell on
drivable area, walkway or crossing (coverage >= 0.3): the rest stand on grass, in parks, car parks or where the map has no walkway; ground plane = box bottom more than
0.5 m above or below the ego ground plane within 40 m (hills, overpasses: a limit for a flat-ground camera lift, not an error of the box); visible boxes marked occluded =
boxes the annotators rate 80-100 % visible whose centre cell lies in our occlusion mask; ego off the map = fewer than half of the cells just in front of the ego car are drivable.
Findings

Map holes: the ego car is off the map road in 45 of 9246 keyframes (0.49%), in 5 sequences, all Boston Seaport: scene-0502 (17), scene-0517 (11), scene-0499 (7), scene-0515 (6), scene-0501 (4) (Pier 4 construction area).
Moving vehicles off the drivable area: 247 of 10127 (2.4%); the ten worst sequences hold 48% of them
(scene-0357 24, scene-0397 17, scene-0131 16, scene-0361 13, scene-0133 9, scene-0358 9). In the two sequences inspected (scene-0131, 0361) they are cars on elevated roads, box bottoms
2-3 m above the ego road, which the 2D drivable area does not contain; the others were not inspected.

Pedestrians: 88% of the Boston pedestrians stand on a map surface, but only 72% (One-North) and 66% (Holland Village): the Singapore maps have fewer walkway polygons, and people stand in car parks and on grass - so a pedestrian head must not rely on 'walkway' as a prior.
Unknown velocity ('short track'): 0.4% of the observed boxes; radar override 0.10%, conflict 0.013%.

Speed: 31 keyframes have a box faster than 60 km/h, 1 faster than 80 km/h; mean 9.6 observed boxes and 1.1 moving vehicles per keyframe: most of the scene is static, which is why the loss must balance moving and static cells.

pages.title: Qualitative review: what the pictures show
lines: What I saw in the pictures (21 four-panel examples and 7 close-ups were inspected one by one, the thumbnails as a whole)
Right:
- Boxes enclose the real objects in all close-ups: cars at 5-30 m, a walking pedestrian, a group of about 12 people at a Singapore junction boxed person by person, a
van behind a parked row, cars behind bushes. In rain with a wet lens and at night the boxes are as good: the GT does not use the image.
- Map lines follow the road geometry in every close-up; where paint is visible (3 Boston close-ups: dashed lane divider, faded double yellow in rain, the road centre line) the line lies
on it within about 0.1-0.3 m. Lane-connector centre-lines turn correctly through junctions (they are map arcs, not paint, so they cross painted areas).
- Parked rows are stationary (white rim, zero velocity), moving cars carry arrows and km/h that match the lane direction (oncoming lanes point toward the ego car).
- Thumbnails of 96 random keyframes (2 sheets): roads, junctions, crossings, car parks and ramps look like the scene; objects sit on the roads and in the car parks.
Wrong or doubtful:
- Map holes: scene-0501 has an EMPTY map under the ego car on a marked road; scene-0499 has a single grey blob and no lane lines (construction zone).
- Roads outside the 2D map: scene-0131 / scene-0361 have cars at 38-55 km/h on elevated roads (box bottoms 2.2-2.8 m above the ego road) that the drivable area
does not contain, so they look 'off the drivable area'.
- Occlusion mask: in dense car parks (scene-0382, 0395) and behind buses (scene-0236, 0286) the 2D mask hides everything behind the first row, including boxes the annotators
list as visible; it is a conservative mask, not a visibility ground truth.
- Height: scene-0128 has a vehicle of 80 km/h whose box bottom is 1.7 m above the ego road: it hangs above the road in the image (an elevated road behind a fence);
the GT is 3D and consistent, a flat-ground image lift would put it in the wrong place.
- Two oncoming cars of 73 and 81 km/h in scene-0094 stand outside the camera view; the 81 km/h one is radar-corrected, neither can be checked by eye.
- Ignored boxes (scene-0236: 46) are objects behind the bus without a lidar / radar point: they are neither object nor free space, which is right, but a lot of area in a busy street.

notes.scene-0033_k06: Observed: sparse Singapore road, one car 30 m ahead - the box sits on it; lane dividers (yellow) and centre-lines (cyan, with direction arrows) follow the lane. An easy keyframe: the GT is almost empty.
notes.scene-0321_k24: Observed: Boston junction with 13 vehicles and 8 pedestrians. Parked row at the left = stationary (white rim), moving cars carry arrows and km/h, pedestrians on the crossing. The blue occluded area behind the white truck at the left is large.
notes.scene-0499_k12: Observed (random draw): a MAP HOLE. The map has one grey blob and no lane dividers or centre-lines for this construction street; the camera panel shows no map lines. Boxes (workers, parked cars) are fine.
notes.scene-0238_k02: Selected by: busiest Boston keyframe. Full-resolution close-up on a later page: boxes enclose the SUV and the sedan, the pedestrians at the far crossing, lane-connector centre-lines turn through the junction.
notes.scene-0276_k10: Selected by: busiest One-North keyframe. Close-up on a later page: a group of about 12 people at the left is boxed person by person, cars at the right.
notes.scene-0317_k02: Observed: Queenstown, bus ahead, a row of pedestrians along the kerb (27 pedestrians), roundabout lanes in the map. Large occluded wedge behind the bus; moving car at 20 km/h far ahead.
notes.scene-1077_k08: Observed: night on a big Singapore road; all 17 vehicles are boxed although the image is dark; the oncoming lanes (right) carry arrows toward the ego car at 30-65 km/h, the car ahead in the ego lane moves away at 42 km/h.
notes.scene-1094_k10: Observed: night after rain, 38 pedestrians and 3 scooters at a junction: the GT is as dense as by day, pedestrians boxed individually; lane connectors cross the junction.
notes.scene-0479_k02: Observed: rain, wet lens, Boston street with 42 vehicles and 31 pedestrians. Parked rows are stationary; slow queueing cars at the right bottom have small non-zero velocities (dark red in the motion panel), the car 33 m ahead moves at 32 km/h.
notes.scene-0441_k20: Observed: heavy rain / mist; the road divider (orange) follows the faded yellow dashes (close-up page), cars in the car parks on both sides are boxed.
notes.scene-0323_k14: Observed: pedestrians crossing at a Boston crosswalk (51 pedestrians): the walking man and the groups at the far fence are boxed; the motion panel shows pedestrians as small slow dots.
notes.scene-0538_k36: Observed: a park next to the road, 43 pedestrians (most on a surface the map does not have as walkway: right side black), parked scooters (orange). The ped boxes are many and small; occluded wedges behind parked scooters.
notes.scene-0094_k00: Observed: Boston wide road. Two oncoming cars (73 and 81 km/h, the 81 km/h one radar-corrected) are outside the camera view. Close-up on a later page: the lane divider lies on the dashed paint within about 0.15 m.
notes.scene-0128_k34: Observed: the 80 km/h vehicle (25 m ahead, 22 m left; its box moved 0.78 m to the camera time) has its box bottom 1.7 m above the ego road: it hangs above the road in the image (an elevated road behind the fence). The 3D GT is consistent, a flat-ground lift would misplace it.
notes.scene-0200_k10: Observed (close-up on a later page): the orange road divider lies on the painted double yellow line within about 0.2 m; the stationary cars at the right and the van ahead are boxed one by one.
notes.scene-0194_k14: Selected by: most radar-conflict flags. A flagged track keeps its annotation velocity (flag '!' in the objects panel when drawn in range). Singapore curve with two bicycles lying on the grass (orange) and a moving car 20 km/h.
notes.scene-0286_k38: Observed: radar overrides ('o' next to the km/h labels): the radar fixed the track speed of boxes at the intersection; the big bus at the right is boxed and occludes most of the right half of the BEV.
notes.scene-0284_k38: Selected by: most 'short track' boxes (velocity unknown: weight 0 in flow_weight, box NOT moved to the camera time). They are not marked in the picture. Boston street, 25 stationary boxes along the kerb: the velocity panel is black.
notes.scene-0030_k08: Selected by: highest share of boxes off the ego ground plane (> 0.5 m); the picture looks right (curving road, parked scooters, many ignored pedestrian boxes at the left).
notes.scene-0168_k00: Observed (off-plane pick): a long row of parked cars in a car park at the right, all stationary; the car park polygon (blue-grey) contains them. Nothing wrong in the GT.
notes.scene-0382_k06: Observed (occlusion pick): dense Singapore car park with 50 stationary vehicles; the 2D occlusion mask (blue) marks everything behind the first row, although many of those boxes are rated visible by the annotators. Yellow = ignored boxes without a point.
notes.scene-0395_k18: Observed (occlusion pick): Boston car park left and right of the road; cells between the parked cars are marked occluded (blue) - conservative, not a visibility truth.
notes.scene-0131_k08: Observed (off-road pick): three cars at 48-51 km/h with box bottoms 2.2-2.7 m above the ego road: an elevated road, not in the 2D drivable area (the right half of the BEV is black). A map limit, not a box error.
notes.scene-0361_k04: Observed (off-road pick): moving cars (38-55 km/h) on an elevated road beyond the grass strip (box bottoms 2.2-2.8 m above the ego road); the drivable area ends before them.
notes.scene-0236_k10: Observed (ignored pick): busy Boston street with 32 pedestrians; 46 boxes have no lidar / radar point (yellow dots at the left, behind the bus). They are ignored, neither object nor free space.
notes.scene-0501_k32: Observed (ego-off-map pick): a MAP HOLE: the ego car stands on a marked road but the map has no drivable area, no dividers and no centre-lines in range; the BEV panel is empty. 0.5 % of the keyframes are like this; leave them out of the map loss.

tail.title: What this overview does not show, and what to do about it
lines: Not verified (no independent truth on disk)
- The positions and sizes of the boxes: they are the nuScenes annotations; no lidar point cloud is available to re-measure them. Annotation noise stays in the GT.
- The box shift to the camera time: direction and size checked with raw radar positions only; at the real 36 ms the three variants (annotation / camera / opposite) are within noise there.
- Velocity across the line of sight: the radar measures the radial part only; the tangential part is the annotation's.
- The other five cameras: their offsets to the annotation time were not measured (front camera only); the GT is defined in the front-camera frame.
- Night and rain beyond three mini sequences and 45 daytime rain sequences: the rebuild will bring them into the same table.
Recommendations for use (they are also in autogt/AGENTS.md)
1. Leave keyframes with the ego car off the map (drivable_area[2:8, 50:54].mean() < 0.5, 0.3-0.5 %) out of the map loss; do not read 'no road' as 'free space' there.
2. Treat the occlusion mask as soft: do not zero the object loss behind a box for boxes the annotators call visible (visibility '4').
3. Balance moving and static cells in every velocity loss; report errors split by moving / static with the zero predictor next to them.
4. Compare models only on the same GT signature; the signature 15efbde2d1 is the camera-time GT.
5. For a headline number on boxes use `boxes_at='annotation'` additionally if the comparison is against nuScenes-style evaluation.
Possible next steps (not started)
- a per-keyframe `map_valid` flag in meta (ego off the map / drivable layer empty) so that nobody has to re-derive it;
- a lidar or scene-flow check of boxes and velocities if the lidar sweeps are downloaded (needs the user's OK);
- the other five cameras' time offsets, if a multi-camera GT is wanted.
